blocks.text: THE girl leads the morning prayer in a voice that reaches the back of the hall, her hands folded, her eyes shut, her name withheld from this story by the same law that lawmakers now want to rewrite. Behind her, more than a hundred children answer in unison. They sound like any campus at seven in the morning. Someone stumbles over a line of the chaplet and gets elbowed. Someone laughs and swallows it. The morning moves the way school mornings move. The children sweep. They line up.
